prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B013 is the one candidate on which all six openings agree, and the agreement rests on substance rather than habit. The chain runs from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), through receptor biology and the gut-pancreas axis, to long-acting agonists with large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is understood, the impact is very large and still growing, and decades of confirmation make the recognition mature rather than premature. Holst (native GLP-1 physiology), Drucker (receptor biology and translational framing) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) cover the discovery side of the chain as a coherent trio.
statement.case_against: The attribution is crowded and a three-person cap forces an exclusion that some will regard as unfair: Knudsen, whose acylated analogues (liraglutide, then semaglutide) made the biology a drug, and Habener, who is outside the supplied credit. Mojsov's role is also disputed in discussion, and I have not verified priority claims. A prize that stops at hormone discovery risks looking detached from the therapy that changed medicine, while one that includes drug development blurs the line between physiology and industrial optimisation. B013 is also so far ahead that unanimity could hide the attribution problem.

responses.point: Perlmann names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Knudsen's long-acting analogues as what turned the biology into a drug, and regards Mojsov's contribution as credited but disputed.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen argument seriously, since without acylated analogues the physiology would not have reached patients, and it is the strongest case for the other trio. I still keep Mojsov in place of Knudsen because the citation I propose honours a discovery of physiology, and peptide identification and synthesis of the active form sits upstream of any analogue. I accept that her priority is contested and that I cannot resolve it from the file. If the committee finds that the Mojsov credit does not hold up, I would move to Knudsen rather than leave the slot empty.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius also names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, argues that Mojsov's contribution is a real credit question a three-person cap cannot resolve, and stresses the size of the translational impact.
responses.response: We agree on the size of the impact and on Drucker and Holst. Our disagreement is whether the third name should be a discoverer or a developer, and it is narrower than it looks, since both of us see that one of the two is excluded. I would not use the translational payoff to justify the third name, because that reasoning would apply to many industrial contributors. The committee should decide the principle first, discovery or development, and let the name follow.

responses.point: Sandberg ranks B010, the HPV virus-like particle vaccines, second, citing a rare case of a vaccine directly preventing cancer with population-level evidence, and ranks B042 third.
responses.response: I agree that B010 is mature and consequential, and that the population data on cervical precancer and cancer incidence are strong evidence for a preventive effect. My reservation is attribution rather than merit: the VLP work involved parallel groups, a deceased co-inventor cannot be credited, and priority between Lowy and Schiller on one side and Frazer on the other is not something I can verify. I rank it fifth for that reason. If Sandberg can argue that the three names are cleanly separable, I would move it above B042.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics (B025) third, as a circuit neuroscientist, calling its methodological impact transformative while admitting that its medical impact is mainly as a research tool so far.
responses.response: I share the admiration for optogenetics, and I agree that the medical impact is limited as yet. I would go further than El-Manira: with six credited names and a three-person cap, any configuration excludes Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck, who each have a strong claim, so the problem is not only maturity but also fairness. As a tool, it also differs in kind from a disease-mechanism contribution. I would keep it as a later candidate rather than an alternative this year.

uncertainties: Whether the Mojsov credit survives scrutiny of priority claims, and whether Knudsen should replace her.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise hormone discovery alone or also drug design, and how Habener's omission from the supplied credit should be weighed.
Whether CAR-T (B042) credit can be settled without Eshhar, who is outside the supplied names, if the committee prefers a second prize part.
Long-term safety and outcome data for obesity indications are still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted ballot. My co-authored work on spatial transcriptomics (Science 2016) and my single-cell and brain-atlas work do not involve the GLP-1, CAR-T or antisense candidates, and I have not checked any co-authorship with their credited names. I would recuse if a credited name turned out to be a close collaborator.
